title: A more practical mood editor
question: Reworked around the references: choose sounds, balance the mix, test, then save. These are preparation layouts—not the live soundboard. All keep Soundscape’s existing dark visual language and 3–6-layer focus.

options.label: Choose sounds, then shape the mix
options.thesis: Give finding sounds and balancing them their own focused views, with the current mood always in sight.
options.viewport: Choose sounds opens with the searchable library across the left and the current mood’s five sounds at right; Shape mix switches the work area to volume, pan, loop, and fade controls without losing the selection.
options.risk: Clear for starting a mood, but switching views adds a step when repeatedly auditioning and adjusting layers.

options.label: Sound rows with in-place editing
options.thesis: Choose a sound, set its level, test the mood; expand only the layer that needs more detail.
options.viewport: Scene and mood selectors above one spacious layer list; every row has audition, volume, mute, solo, and playback state; the selected row opens pan and fades in place; Preview mix and Save mood stay in the bottom bar.
options.risk: Only one layer’s detailed settings are open at a time; rows below it move when it expands.

options.label: A compact channel mixer
options.thesis: Balance the entire atmosphere at once with one consistent strip per sound, rather than artwork cards.
options.viewport: A scene/mood header above five sound channels and an Add sound slot; each channel exposes source, pan, vertical level, loop, fades, mute and solo; a shared preview bar anchors the screen.
options.risk: Great for comparing levels, but more audio-tool-like and less comfortable for long filenames or narrow windows.
